title: AFL Players Salary List: How Hourly Rates Convert to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Explore the AFL players salary list and learn how to convert hourly rates to annual pay using the 38-hour week. Includes minimum wage, award rates, tax, and super.
salarySummary: Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming a standard 38-hour week for full-time employees.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate?
faqs.a: Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, casual loading brings it to $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for lack of paid leave.

faqs.q: How does the AFL players salary list compare to typical wages?
faqs.a: AFL players are paid under a collective bargaining agreement with total player payments per club, not hourly rates. The 2023–2027 CBA sets limits per club, with minimum payments for drafted players. This differs from hourly or annual salary structures for most workers.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you know your hourly rate, converting it to an annual figure helps you compare job offers, budget, and plan for tax and super. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For full-time employees, the typical week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you work part-time or casual, use your actual weekly hours.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the base rate for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most workers, however, are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, listing minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour. The loading is paid instead of entitlements like sick leave and annual leave. Our [the timesheet](/) includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically.

### Superannuation and Tax

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute an extra $9,600 into your super fund.

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page shows how these deductions affect your net pay.

### The AFL Players Salary List

While most Australians are paid by the hour or a fixed annual salary, professional AFL players operate under a different system. The AFL and AFLW Collective Bargaining Agreement 2023–2027 sets total player payments per club, not individual hourly rates. The document outlines that each club must spend at least 95% of its total player payment limit on players. These payments include base salaries, match payments, and additional services agreements.

For example, a first-year draftee in 2023 might receive a minimum payment, while established stars earn much more. The AFL players salary list is not publicly itemised per player, but the aggregate club limits are published. This structure contrasts with the hourly or annual salary models used in most industries. If you are comparing your pay to an AFL player’s, remember that their compensation includes match payments, image rights, and superannuation, and is not directly comparable to an hourly rate.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage:

- Weekly: $1004.90
- Fortnightly: $2009.80

After tax and Medicare, your take-home will be lower. Use our [reference tables](/data) to see estimates for different income levels.

### Putting It All Together

Whether you are on the National Minimum Wage, an award rate, or a salary, the conversion from hourly to annual is straightforward. Always check your award or agreement for the correct minimum rate. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page provides more examples, and the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains when the 25% loading applies.

Remember that super is paid on top of your gross pay, so your total employment cost is higher than your salary. Tax estimates are based on the 2026–27 rates and the Medicare levy. For a precise calculation, use our [the timesheet](/) tool, which lets you enter your hourly rate, add casual loading, and see annual, fortnightly, and monthly figures along with estimated tax and super.

### Key Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary-time earnings were $2083.70 in May 2026. This is much higher than the National Minimum Wage because it includes all full-time employees, many of whom are on award or above-award rates. When you see an “average” salary, remember it reflects a mix of industries and experience levels. Your own rate depends on your award classification, skills, and location.

For a complete picture of your pay, always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) and the Fair Work Commission’s [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice and super contributions affect your tax.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
